children: Private-equity firms Shamrock Capital and Flexpoint Ford have acquired Podium Entertainment, a book publisher focused on independent authors and audiobooks, for north of $400 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

Podium is known for publishing and introducing additional formats for romantasy and science fiction titles from writers who originally self-published their work, including "Quicksilver" author Callie Hart and Shirtaloon, who is behind the series "He Who Fights With Monsters."
Shamrock and Flexpoint Ford bought Podium from private-equity firm Presidio Investors, which had acquired the publisher in 2019.
As part of the deal, music rights company GoldState Music has also made a minority investment in Podium, the people said.
David Kaefer, previously head of audiobooks and music at Spotify, will join a new Podium board, and Podium's existing management team will remain in place.

Podium started in 2013, as authors were increasingly publishing their own works through Amazon.com's Kindle Direct service. The company initially licensed the audio rights to self-published ebooks, and has since expanded into other aspects of publishing, including helping independent authors distribute ebooks on Amazon and printed books in bricks-and-mortar shops.
Presidio Investors invested in technology to identify trending books ripe for acquisition, and Podium now has a catalog of 15,000 titles.

Shamrock's media holdings include investments in content catalogs with songs by Beyoncé, Coldplay and Rihanna, as well as films and videogames. It previously owned Taylor Swift's master recordings but sold the catalog back to the pop star in 2025.

Flexpoint Ford has an investment in GoldState Music, which acquires and manages copyrights for songs by artists including Sheryl Crow and Florida Georgia Line, as well as Create Music Group, which provides services to independent artists.

Audiobooks are among the hottest corners of the publishing industry. Annual revenue from digital audiobook sales topped $1 billion in 2025, up from $265 million for 2016, according to the Association of American Publishers.

Meanwhile, independent authors who bypass agents and traditional publishing houses have gained traction in the #BookTok era, with self-published projects turning into global bestsellers through word-of-mouth.
